key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks identify tensegrity prestress across taut–slack transitions, which can reveal member parameters that taut-only records leave undetermined.
engineering_relevance: The method supports prestress monitoring in tensegrity structures, where tension loss can alter stability, stiffness, and dynamic response.
method: Train networks on equation-of-motion residuals in constrained Cartesian coordinates.
Jointly identify force densities, damping, and axial stiffness while retaining tension-only cable behavior.
Use Fisher-information analysis before inversion to assess parameter identifiability.
evidence_signal: Tests on simulated frames and a 3D prism plus two measured systems yielded force-density errors within 1.5% for identifiable one-module parameters, 4.2% median error for five modules, and 2.9% RMS agreement with measured simplex prestress.
watch_item: Parameter recovery depends on sensor coverage and excitation; check identifiability before interpreting estimates for individual members.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions
